subject: UAT benchmark roadmap & TTFT streaming plan (MAP draft)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Rao <priya.ra o@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: UAT benchmark roadmap & TTFT streaming plan (MAP draft)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our mutual action plan (attached draft), we want to align on a short UAT benchmark cadence that will validate two things before we proceed to Dedicated capacity:

- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for chat generation under streaming (target p50/p95/p99)
- End-to-end streaming latency and stable throughput at 8, 16 and 32 concurrent sessions

Attached is a short plan (llm-ttft-plan.pdf) that lays out: scheduling, traffic shape, data redaction notes, and pass/fail criteria. High level timeline we propose:

1) Week 0 (this week): finalize MAP & share seed prompts and sample traffic
2) Week 1: Redwood runs baseline lab runs (single-region, baseline model w/ standard KV cache)
3) Week 2: Customer UAT with Redwood-observed traffic + shared dashboard
4) Week 3: Remediation + final sign-off / capacity recommendation

Pass/fail example (TTFT streaming): p50 < 120ms, p95 < 320ms, p99 < 620ms for 2-token-first response under our streaming runtime when running at target concurrency. These values are suggestions; happy to adjust to match LumenHealth SLAs.

Can you confirm: (a) target concurrency you want us to test in UAT (8/16/32), and (b) a 1-hour block next week for the joint run where your networking and tokenization folks can monitor?

I've CC'd Karthik to help coordinate test harness and credentials.

Thanks,

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: llm-ttft-plan.pdf, mutual-action-plan.docx
From: Priya Rao <priya.ra o@lumenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenHealth Platform Team <platform@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: UAT benchmark roadmap & TTFT streaming plan (MAP draft)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear plan and the suggested pass/fail thresholds. Quick answers:

- Concurrency: please test at 8 and 24 (we want to understand both a conservative and a stressed baseline).
- Joint run: we can do Thu 14 Oct 14:00–15:00 PT. Please confirm.

A couple of asks before the run:
1) Can you share the exact sample payload (we'll scrub PHI) and the JSON schema for streaming messages so our tokenization folks can pre-validate?
2) We have a networking constraint: egress to Redwood's test runner must come from our VPC range 10.18.0.0/16; can you confirm the test runner IP list you will use?

On pass/fail thresholds, our SREs are comfortable with p50 < 150ms, p95 < 350ms, p99 < 700ms for now. If Redwood's baseline is consistently better, we'll ask for updated SLAs in the MAP.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—Priya Rao
Director, Platform Engineering | LumenHealth
priya.ra o@lumenhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: UAT benchmark roadmap & TTFT streaming plan (internal sync)

Team —

Quick internal sync before we lock the test harness for 10/14:

- Traffic shape: Priya asked for 8 and 24 concurrent sessions. We'll run three phases: 8 steady-state, 24 ramp to 24 over 90s, and 24 sustained for 15 minutes.
- Model variant: run v2-compat small quantized variant and v3-ffi baseline. Report will include both.
- Metrics we will collect: TTFT (token 1 latency), streaming token latencies (p50/p95/p99 per token position 1/5/10), end-to-end response completion time, throughput (tokens/sec), CPU/GPU utilization, memory, and network RTTs.
- Data handling: all customer-provided prompts must be redacted; we will run on anonymized payloads and share the scrubbed dataset.
- IPs: set up test runner in our staging cluster; will publish ephemeral CIDR list 48 hours before the run.

Ben — can you scope the test runner config and confirm whether we need a GPU isolated node for the 24 concurrent sustained run (I'd prefer isolated GPU to avoid noisy neighbors).

Monica — please prepare the shared Grafana dashboard and include token-level waterfall charts we can export to CSV.

I'll glue together the MAP doc and push a revision to Drive by EOD.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Revised MAP + baseline run results (attached)

Priya —

Thanks — confirmed for Thu 14 Oct 14:00–15:00 PT (we'll send calendar invite once we finalize CIDRs). I've attached: (1) updated mutual-action-plan.docx with the final test window and sign-off criteria, and (2) a short CSV (streaming-raw-results.csv) with our baseline lab run numbers for quick review. Highlights from baseline:

- Single-region lab baseline (v3-ffi): p50 TTFT = 98 ms, p95 TTFT = 270 ms, p99 TTFT = 590 ms
- 8 concurrent (steady): p50 token latency = 110 ms, p95 = 300 ms, p99 = 580 ms
- 24 concurrent (ramp then sustain): p50 token latency = 170 ms, p95 = 420 ms, p99 = 820 ms (we observed occasional spikes tied to KV cache warmup)
- Throughput: sustained ~4.7k tokens/sec at 24 concurrent on the chosen instance type

Action items we propose before joint run:
- Redwood: publish ephemeral CIDR list + test runner creds by Tue 12 Oct EOD
- LumenHealth: provide scrubbed sample payload and confirm VPC egress rule
- Joint: 60-minute run 14 Oct with monitoring window and quick post-run sync

If these baseline numbers look reasonable against your SRE thresholds (Priya mentioned p50 < 150, p95 < 350, p99 < 700), we should flag the 24-concurrency p99 as a point for remediation (cache priming + slightly higher instance class).

Thanks — attaching the CSV and updated MAP.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

Attachments: streaming-raw-results.csv, mutual-action-plan.docx

Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Revised MAP + baseline run results (ack & next steps)

Marissa / Team —

Thanks for the detailed notes and the baseline CSV. We reviewed with SRE; summary:

- 8-concurrency numbers look fine.
- 24-concurrency p99 = 820 ms is above our tolerance; we want Redwood to try cache-priming and a brief warmup run as part of the joint session.
- Please include memory/GPU-util samples in the run output we can archive for compliance.

We are good to proceed with the 14 Oct run assuming the warmup step is in the test plan and we get the CIDRs by Tue EOD. Post-run, we'll have a 30-minute follow-up call the same day for sign-off; if performance is within our adjusted bar we will move ahead with a Dedicated capacity purchase and finalize the MAP.

Priya
Priya Rao
Director, Platform Engineering | LumenHealth
